questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three structural problems with a training script run by hand?
options: It has no schedule
It has no dependency management between steps
It has no failure handling
It cannot be written in Python
questions.explain: The language a script is written in isn't the problem — the missing schedule, dependency guarantees, and failure handling are what a pipeline framework supplies.

questions.q: In Apache Airflow, what is a DAG?
options: A type of database used only for storing metrics
A directed acyclic graph of tasks with explicit, one-way dependencies, defined in Python
A Kubernetes-specific container format
A deprecated Airflow feature replaced by components
questions.explain: Airflow models every workflow as a DAG — tasks connected by explicit dependencies that only flow in one direction.

questions.q: What is the key structural difference between an Airflow task and a Kubeflow Pipelines component?
options: There is no difference — they are the same concept with different names
A Kubeflow component always runs independently containerized, while an Airflow task typically runs as a Python callable against shared infrastructure
Airflow components always run on Kubernetes, while Kubeflow tasks never do
Kubeflow components cannot have dependencies on each other
questions.explain: Kubeflow Pipelines containerizes every step by default, giving strong portability; Airflow is more general-purpose and doesn't containerize each task by default.

questions.q: What distinguishes a training pipeline from an inference (serving) pipeline?
options: A training pipeline is bounded and batch-shaped, producing a model version; an inference pipeline is continuous or request-driven, producing predictions
A training pipeline never has a schedule
An inference pipeline always runs on a fixed daily cron schedule
There is no meaningful difference between the two
questions.explain: Training pipelines have a clear start and end and output a model version; inference pipelines are either always running or triggered per request, and output predictions, not models.

questions.q: Which tool is described as being built on top of Argo Workflows under the hood?
options: Apache Airflow
Metaflow
Kubeflow Pipelines
Prefect
questions.explain: Kubeflow Pipelines is Kubernetes-native and is built on top of Argo Workflows, which it uses more generally for ML-specific, containerized pipelines.
